I tidied up `0.html` without changing how it looks on a normal screen: it is still a black 400px circle centred on the page. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

- **No stray horizontal scrollbar:** removed `width: 100vw` from `body`, which overflows whenever a vertical scrollbar is present.
- **Better mobile centring:** `body` now uses `min-height: 100dvh` (with `100vh` as a fallback), so the circle stays centred when mobile browser toolbars show or hide.
- **Circle scales down on small screens:** the SVG is now `min(400px, 100vmin)` wide with a 1:1 aspect ratio, so it shrinks to fit instead of being clipped on viewports under 400px.
- **Screen reader label:** added `role="img"` and `aria-label="Circle"` to the SVG. If the circle is purely decorative, swap these for `aria-hidden="true"`.
- **Minor hygiene:** added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset and `display: block` on the SVG.

I left the title and the `id` as `ae683f770`, since they look like generated identifiers. "Improve" was open-ended, so I kept to fixes and did not touch colour, dark mode or animation.

I tidied `0.html` without changing how it looks in light mode: it is still a centred circle, at most 400px wide. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

## What changed

- **Dark mode:** the page now follows the system colour scheme, and the circle takes the text colour. It shows black on white in light mode and light on dark in dark mode.
- **Mobile sizing:** the circle's width now uses `100dvmin`, with `100vmin` as a fallback, so it isn't clipped in landscape when the browser toolbar is showing.
- **Simpler CSS:** I replaced the universal `*` reset with `margin: 0` on `body`, which is all this page needs. I also dropped `display: block`, `height: auto` and `aspect-ratio` from the SVG, since the `viewBox` already keeps it square.

## What I left alone

The `<title>` is still `ae683f770`, which matches the SVG `id` and looks generated, so I kept it in case something depends on it. If nothing does, a readable title such as "Circle" would be better for tabs, bookmarks and screen readers.

I made two small changes to `0.html`; the page was already in good shape, so I kept the edits light. I haven't opened it in a browser to check the result.

- **Favicon added:** an inline SVG favicon of the same circle, which turns white in dark mode. This also stops the browser requesting a missing `/favicon.ico`.
- **Centering simplified:** the body now uses `display: grid; place-items: center` instead of the three flex declarations. The layout is the same.

The title `ae683f770` matches the SVG's `id`, so I treated it as a deliberate identifier and left it alone. If it's a placeholder, a readable title would help in tabs, bookmarks and screen readers.

The circle also touches the viewport edges on screens narrower than 400px. Changing the width to something like `min(400px, 90dvmin)` would give it a margin, but that alters the look, so I left it.
